messages:
felix: hey all, second-day blocker. running the dev compose and trying to enable TimescaleDB extension during migrations. db container exits during init with: "ERROR: could not access file "$libdir/timescaledb"" and then "FATAL: extension "timescaledb" is not supported by this installation"

nina: welcome! that usually means the postgres image you're using doesn't have timescaledb built in. are you on alpine by chance?

felix: yes, compose uses `image: postgres:15-alpine` from the quickstart.

omar: alpine images are small but miss many contrib extensions. two quick options: 1) use an official timescaledb image like `timescale/timescaledb-postgis:pg15-2.13.2` or similar, 2) build a custom image FROM `postgres:15` (debian) and install timescaledb before initdb.

felix: switched to `timescale/timescaledb:pg15` and the extension error is gone, nice. but then I hit another thing: our repo mounts `./docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` into the container so we can run SQL on init. when using a host mount the init scripts sometimes fail with "permission denied" during container startup.

nina: host mount perms again. on mac with Colima or Docker Desktop the host UID/GID mapping can make files owned by an unexpected user. ensure the scripts are readable/executable by the container user (usually 1000 or postgres uid 999). `chmod -R a+rX ./docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` on host usually helps.

omar: also ensure your init scripts don't rely on being run as root. the entrypoint runs them as postgres user. if you need to run privileged setup, build it into the image or use a one-off `docker compose run --rm db bash` step.

felix: did `chmod -R a+rX` and recompose and that fixed the init scripts. last hiccup: I accidentally set `network_mode: host` on the db for testing, and then the app container couldn't reach `db` hostname anymore (app said "could not translate host name "db"").

nina: yes `network_mode: host` bypasses the compose network and DNS, so service hostnames don't resolve. avoid it for the dev compose unless you really need host networking.

felix: everything green now: 1) use timescale image for TimescaleDB extensions, 2) make init scripts readable/executable and owned/mapped correctly, 3) avoid network_mode: host so compose DNS works. big help, thanks!

infra-bot: Note: added TimescaleDB + init script checklist to dev-setup: prefer Timescale images for extensions, ensure initdb scripts are readable/executable, avoid host network for compose stacks: https://go.redwood/dev-setup (:book:)

docs-bot: Suggested quickstart tweak: update example compose to use `timescale/timescaledb:pg15` with comment about local-dev choice; filing PR: https://go.redwood/pull/3214

felix: will add to my onboarding notes and ping @nina for a follow-up on the quickstart. thanks everyone! :rocket:
